stem: Meera's teacher asks why solar calendars add a leap day about every four years. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A leap day is added because the Moon takes exactly 28 days to orbit the Earth.
Earth takes nearly 365.25 days to revolve around the Sun, so the extra quarter-days add up to about one full day every four years, and the leap day keeps the calendar aligned with the seasons.
Calendars have 365 days by rule, and leap years are just arbitrary extra days chosen by governments.
A leap day is added to correct the time Earth takes to spin once on its axis.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's revolution takes nearly 365.25 days, slightly more than 365; the accumulated extra hours make roughly one day every four years, and a leap day restores the calendar's alignment with the seasons. Only B states this. A confuses lunar motion with the solar year, C treats leap years as arbitrary rather than corrective, and D confuses rotation with revolution.
